free_tier.stated: Personal is USD 0 forever: 'Unlimited use with your API keys or external agents like Claude Agent, Codex CLI, and more'; the vendor serves no hosted model and no edit predictions on this plan
free_tier.notes: the editor imposes no quota of its own; the tokens come from the user's own keys or from the external agent's own plan

per_object_cap.stated: not applicable: a coding editor meters nothing itself

egress.terms: not applicable: the chosen endpoint serves the inference

interface_detail: a desktop editor with an Agent Panel; a keys-and-environment headless path exists as the eval-cli binary of the zed repository, run with --workdir, --model, --instruction, --timeout and --output-dir, which writes result.json, thread.md and thread.json to the output directory. External agents attach over the Agent Client Protocol (ACP), which the interface vocabulary has no term for
tooling: the user installs and runs the Zed editor, or builds and runs the eval-cli binary from the zed repository with cargo, on a rented or free machine; provider keys come from environment variables such as ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY and OPENROUTER_API_KEY, and the External Agents installed from the ACP Registry (Claude, Codex, OpenCode, Copilot, Cursor, Pi Coding Agent) own their own auth and billing. Remote Development runs a Zed headless server over SSH, but the UI and the model calls stay on the local machine
chaining: the editor is a front end for keys from inference/ and for agents that carry their own plans, such as Claude Agent and Codex, so it adds no quota of its own to a stack; the hosted Zed models are the separate paid record zed-pro
limits_note: the editor carries no vendor-imposed usage cap on this plan, since the vendor serves no inference through it; the ceiling is the endpoint the keys or the external agent point to
binding_note: nothing binds in the editor itself; the endpoint's quota decides capacity

identity_cost.detail: no account for the editor or for AI on the user's own API keys: the docs say signing in is not required. Sign-in, needed only for Zed-hosted models and collaboration, is GitHub OAuth with the read:user scope, and the account email is the GitHub one

reliability_note: no reliability event recorded; on this plan the editor does not serve hosted models or edit predictions, and edit predictions from other providers such as GitHub Copilot or a local model still work
confidence_note: plan, sign-in, key and external-agent behaviour are quoted from first-party pages read on 2026-11-02. The eval-cli README is a repository file; the binary itself was not built or run.
